&= \frac{1}{K_i}\sum\limits_{k=1}^{K_i} \mathcal{NN}_{y,i+1,1+d, n}^{\varrho, L, \mathbf{n}}(p_{i+1}^{m,k},\theta_{y,i+1}^*)+hf(t_{i},X_{i}^{\pi,m},\mathcal{NN}_{y,i,1+d, n}^{\varrho, L, \mathbf{n}}(p_{i}^{m},\theta_{y,i}^{r_j}),\mathcal{NN}_{z,i+1,1+d, n\times d}^{\varrho, L, \mathbf{n}}(p_{i}^{m},\theta_{z,i}^*)).

issues.failure_explanation: By (NS-DMC), Y_i = NN_{y,i}(p_i^m,theta*), and S_{y,i} is the K_i-path average of the trained networks NN_{y,i+1}(p_{i+1}^{m,k},theta*) plus hf(t_i,X_i^{pi,m},NN_{y,i}(theta^{r_j}),NN_z(theta*_z)), whereas R^y_{i,2} is defined through the exact simulated quantities (Y_{i+1}^{pi,m,k}=u(t_{i+1},.) and f(.,Y_i^{pi,m},Z_i^{pi,m})). The two sides of the displayed identity are therefore different random variables; they coincide only if the trained networks reproduce the exact discrete solution, which is precisely what the theorem must establish. The same conflation is made for Z (Deep-NN-E-9-1-z), where the display additionally replaces the K_i-path average S_{z,i} by a single increment NN*DeltaW/h, discarding the 1/K_i variance factor; the additive constants thereby produced (e.g. C N from bounding E|NN_{y,i+1}|^2 <= C in (Deep-NN-E-9-3-1)) are dropped in (Deep-NN-E-10) and (Deep-NN-E-16-1). Hence the chain leading to (Deep-NN-E-11) and to the Z-estimate does not prove the stated bound.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Redo the residual accounting: define R^{y/z}_{i,2} with respect to the labels actually fitted (Monte-Carlo averages of the trained networks), keep the factor 1/K_i when bounding E|S_{z,i}-V|^2, retain the additive constants, and bound the deviation between the network labels and the exact simulated labels by the level-(i+1) errors; then restate Theorem ae-DMCE with the corrected residual terms and rerun the Gronwall assembly.
issues.overall_effect: The central L^2 error estimate of the DBR scheme (Theorem ae-DMCE) is not established; the convergence theorem thm:added-1 and the variational-inequality theorem ae-DMCE-R, whose proofs re-use these arguments, lose their support, as do the abstract's and conclusion's claims of rigorous error bounds and half-order convergence.
issues.title: Central error estimate (Theorem ae-DMCE) rests on a false identification of the fitted labels with the exact simulated quantities
issues.why_classification: The repair is a contained re-derivation of the residual accounting (redefined residuals plus Monte-Carlo variance terms) with no new global proof architecture, and a comparable L^2 estimate survives; it exceeds a local routine edit because the statement's residual terms change.

issues.failure_explanation: The displayed chain asserts E|y-NN|^2 = E|(y-NN)1_{<=R}|^2 + E|(y-NN)1_{>R}|^2, which is false ((a+b)^2 differs from a^2+b^2 by the cross term). The tail is then bounded by Hoelder with exponents q and 2q/(2q-1); the reciprocals 1/q + (2q-1)/(2q) = (2q+1)/(2q) do not sum to 1, and the resulting factor P^{(2q-1)/q} is smaller than the conjugate-exponent factor P^{(q-1)/q} that Hoelder provides, so the displayed inequality is stronger than Hoelder licenses. Consequently the R^{-2} tail rate used in (dmce-cr-1) (via (Deep-NN-E-r-7)) is not established by this display.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Redo the tail estimate with conjugate Hoelder exponents, E|(y-NN)^2 1_{>R}| <= ||y-NN||_{2q}^2 P^{(q-1)/q}, and bound P(||X||>R) by Markov with the moment of order 2q/(q-1) (available here since X_0 is deterministic and the coefficients are Lipschitz); the form of (Deep-NN-E-r-7) is then recovered.
issues.overall_effect: The quantitative approximation bound (Deep-NN-E-r-7) and the parameter choice R=O(N^{3/2}), epsilon=O(N^{-3}) used for the half-order convergence claim of Theorem thm:added-1 are unsupported by this step.
issues.title: Truncation/tail approximation estimate in the convergence proof is invalid
issues.why_classification: A local, routine correction of the Hoelder/Markov exponents restores the displayed bound; every substantive claim, the O(h) rate and the complexity formulas are preserved, so no new lemma or weakening is needed.

issues.failure_explanation: Theorem thm:added-1 is obtained by inserting the approximation bounds (Deep-NN-E-r-7)-(Deep-NN-E-r-8) into Theorem ae-DMCE's estimate, whose right-hand side contains the residuals N|R^y_{i+1,2}|^2 + |R^z_{i,2}|^2 + N|R^y_{i+1,1}|^2 + |R^z_{i,1}|^2. The proof never bounds these terms: no Monte-Carlo variance estimate of the form E|R^y_{i,1}|^2, E|R^z_{i,1}|^2 <~ C/(h K_i) is ever derived, no link is established between the fitted residuals R^{y/z}_{i,2} and the population approximation quantities of (Deep-NN-E-r-7)-(Deep-NN-E-r-8) (this would require assuming the training attains the population infimum), and the asserted parameter condition N^2/K = O(1/N) with K = max_i K_i cannot control the sum sum_i N/K_i. The claimed bound max E|Y-Y|^2 + E[sum int |Z-Z|^2] <= Ch is therefore not proved.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the missing nontrivial steps: conditional-variance bounds E|R^y_{i,1}|^2 <~ C/K_i and E|R^z_{i,1}|^2 <~ d/(h K_i); bounds E|R^y_{i,2}|^2 <~ inf_NN E|y_i-NN|^2 + C/K_i (and the z-analogue) linking the residuals to (Deep-NN-E-r-7)-(Deep-NN-E-r-8), with an explicit hypothesis that training attains (approximately) the population infima; and use K = min_i K_i instead of the maximum in (dmce-cr-1).
issues.overall_effect: The advertised half-order convergence rate and the stated complexity/sample-size requirements (grouping size, depth, width, K=O(N^3)) of the DBR scheme are unproven; the theoretical guarantee advertised in the abstract and conclusion is unsupported.
issues.title: Half-order convergence theorem never controls the Monte-Carlo and network-residual terms
issues.why_classification: The missing estimates are standard (Monte-Carlo variance and approximation-residual comparisons) and the O(h) rate and stated complexity survive once they are inserted, so the resolution is contained; but it requires new nontrivial steps and a limited reformulation, exceeding a minor local repair.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: The error estimate for the $Z$-component can be derived using the same arguments as in Steps 3 and 4 of the proof of Theorem \ref{ae-DMCE}; thus, the details are omitted here.

issues.failure_explanation: In the reflected scheme (NS-M-R) the reflected value Y^{pi,m}_{i+1}=max{Ybar^{pi,m}_{i+1},g(X^{pi,m}_{i+1})} enters both conditional expectations defining Ybar^{pi,m}_i and Z^{pi,m}_i. The RDBR losses, however, re-use the Section-3.1 labels S_{y,i}, S_{z,i}, which average the raw networks NN_{y,i+1}(p_{i+1}^{m,k},theta*) without the obstacle; the max appears only afterwards in the output map (NS-DMC-R), so the obstacle never feeds back into the backward induction and the trained networks target the unreflected BSDE. Accordingly the proof's only reflection step, |max(a,c)-max(b,c)| <= |a-b|, cannot close the recursion: the increment (g - NN_{y,i+1})^+ produced by the projection is never estimated, and the Z-component analysis is asserted by reference to the defective Steps 3-4 of Theorem ae-DMCE. The theorem's convergence guarantee for the scheme (NS-DMC-R) as specified is therefore unsupported.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Redefine the RDBR labels to average the reflected sub-values max{NN_{y,i+1}(p_{i+1}^{m,k},theta*), g(X_{i+1}^{pi,m,k})} (for both the Y- and Z-labels), then supply the reflected estimates for the reflection increments (or weaken the theorem to the unreflected setting); at minimum the scheme's labels must match the reflected conditional expectations of (NS-M-R).
issues.overall_effect: The advertised extension of the DBR scheme to variational inequalities (Section 4, Theorem ae-DMCE) is unreliable: the specified RDBR procedure does not solve (eq:VI), and its stated error bound is not established.
issues.title: RDBR scheme's labels omit the reflection, so the variational-inequality convergence claim is unsupported
issues.why_classification: A contained modification of the fitted labels plus standard reflected-BSDE estimates restores a comparable convergence result; the loss is limited but the repair is a nontrivial construction and re-analysis, more than a routine local fix.
